newsitem.title: UK: Competition to whittle down UK insurers - report.
newsitem.headline: Competition to whittle down UK insurers - report.

text.p: A battle for market share at unrealistic prices will cut the number of motor and household underwriters in Britain over the next five years, management consultant Datamonitor said on Monday.

"The losses that the industry has suffered in personal lines will continue into 1997 and the expected upturn in prices will not occur. Many underwriters will be forced to withdraw from mainstreeam personal lines, as the costs of competing in the market continue to rise."
In a report entitled "UK Personal General Insurance 1996", Datamonitor estimates that 30 percent of motor and 20 percent of household underwriters will pull out of the market in the next five years.
The industry is undergoing a structural change as new direct, telephone insurers battle for market share with traditional companies.
"As the structure of the personal general insurance sector changes, so the cost of marketing increases and policy prices fall," Datamonitor said.
"Losses will inevitably result. The market cannot continue to support the number of underwriters that it presently does."
Pressure will be particularly acute on traditional broker-supplied composite insurers from the direct telephone market.
"However, the story will not be one of the inexorable rise of all direct writers, for in this sector only those offering the best service and with a substantial customer base will survive."
A price recovery before 2000 is very unlikely, Datamonitor said, due to the flood of new players.
